The ninth point: sealing the heart does not necessitate patience. Rather, a servant's heart may be sealed and his patience taken from him. Indeed, when the heart is sealed, patience disappears and weakens. This differs from binding (rabt) upon the heart, which does necessitate patience, as Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And He sends down upon you water from the sky to purify you by it, remove from you the defilement of Satan, and strengthen your hearts﴾. In the language, rabt means tying or binding, and so it is said of anyone who endures a matter that he "bound his heart," as if he restrained his heart from agitation. From this comes the expression "he is steadfast of heart" (rabit al-jash).

Al-Wahidi thought that (ʿalā) is superfluous, and that the meaning is "He binds your hearts." That is not what he supposed. There is a clear difference between binding a thing and binding upon it. One says rabata al-faras and al-dabbah (he tied the horse and the animal), and one does not say rabata ʿalayha. When the binding surrounds and covers a thing, it is said rabata ʿalayhi, as if he had encompassed it with the binding. Therefore it is said rabata ʿalā qalbihi, which is more eloquent than saying rabata qalbahu. The point is that with this binding comes stronger and more enduring patience, unlike sealing.

The tenth point: sealing (khatm) is the fastening of the heart so that it does not perceive or understand. It is a barrier preventing knowledge and intention. The Prophet (ﷺ) knew the words of his enemies that he had fabricated the Qur'an, and he perceived them. Allah did not place upon his heart a barrier preventing him from perceiving that or knowing it.

If it is said that the matter is so, but that Allah placed upon his heart a barrier preventing harm from their words, this is more fitting to be called a sealing. Their words did harm him and grieved them, as Allah the Exalted says: ﴿We know that what they say grieves you﴾. The arrival of this harm to him was from Allah's honour toward him, for no prophet was harmed as he was harmed. The interpretation of the verse is the view of Qatadah, and Allah knows best.

Then Allah the Exalted informed that the Qur'an is a reminder (tadhkirah) for the God-fearing (muttaqin), by which the God-fearing one is reminded, sees what benefits him so that he pursues it, and what harms him so that he avoids it. By it he is reminded of the names, attributes and actions of the Lord, so that he believes. By it he is reminded of His reward and punishment, His threat and command, His prohibition, and His signs in His friends and His enemies, in himself, and in what purifies, cleanses and elevates it, and in what corrupts, conceals and debases it. By it he is reminded of the knowledge of origin and return, of Paradise and Hellfire, and of the knowledge of good and evil. It is therefore the reminder in reality, a proof for the worlds and a benefit and guidance for those who seek knowledge.

Then He, glorified is He, said: ﴿And indeed We know that among you are deniers﴾, meaning: they are not hidden from Us, and We will repay them for their denial.

Then Allah the Exalted informed that His Messenger and His speech are a cause of anguish (hasrah) for the disbelievers when they witness the reality of what he reported. Their denial will be among the greatest of their regrets, when regret will no longer benefit them. Thus is every one who denies the truth and affirms falsehood: when the reality of what he denied and affirmed is revealed to him, his denial and affirmation become a regret for him, like one who neglected what would benefit him at the time of acquiring it, until his need for it becomes intense and he witnesses the success of those who attained it, and his neglect becomes a regret upon him.

Then Allah the Exalted informed that the Qur'an and the Messenger are *ḥaqq al-yaqīn* (the sure truth of certainty). It is said that this is of the type of annexing a qualified noun to its quality, meaning "the true certainty," like *masjid al-jāmiʿ* and *ṣalāt al-ūlā*. This point requires verification, so we say, and with Allah is success.

(Section)

Allah the Exalted mentioned in His Book the degrees of certainty (yaqin), and they are three: *ḥaqq al-yaqīn* (the truth of certainty), *ʿilm al-yaqīn* (the knowledge of certainty), and *ʿayn al-yaqīn* (the eye of certainty), as Allah the Exalted says: ﴿No! If you knew with the knowledge of certainty, you would surely see the Hellfire; then you would surely see it with the eye of certainty﴾. These are three degrees of certainty. The first is its knowledge, which is complete affirmation without any doubt or uncertainty that undermines that affirmation, such as the knowledge of certainty about Paradise, for example, and their certainty that it is the abode of the God-fearing and the dwelling of the believers. This is the level of knowledge, like their certainty that the messengers reported it from Allah, and their certainty of the truthfulness of the one who reports.

The second degree is *ʿayn al-yaqīn*, which is the level of seeing and witnessing, as Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Then you would surely see it with the eye of certainty﴾. Between this degree and the one before it there is the difference between knowledge and witnessing: certainty belongs to hearing, and the eye of certainty belongs to sight. In the Musnad of Imam Ahmad, it is related from the Prophet (ﷺ) as a marfūʿ report: "The report is not like one who witnesses it." This is the degree which Abraham the Friend (al-Khalil) asked his Lord to show him, how He gives life to the dead, so that he might attain, alongside knowledge of certainty, the eye of certainty. His request was an increase for himself and a reassurance for his heart, so that the heart is at rest at the moment of witnessing and is content by closing the distance between report and seeing. It is upon this distance that the Prophet used the word "doubt," when he said: "We have more right to doubt than Abraham." Far be it that there was any doubt, either in Abraham or in anyone else. Rather, it is the eye after knowledge, witnessing after report, and sight after hearing.

The third degree is *ḥaqq al-yaqīn*, which is direct contact with a thing through perception of it, as when they enter Paradise and enjoy what is in it. In this world they are at the level of *ʿilm al-yaqīn*; on the Day of Standing, as they draw near and are brought close until they witness it, they are at the level of *ʿayn al-yaqīn*; and when they enter it and experience its bliss, they are at the level of *ḥaqq al-yaqīn*. Direct contact with the known object sometimes occurs through the outward senses and sometimes through the heart. Therefore Allah says: ﴿And indeed, it is the truth of certainty﴾. The heart directly experiences faith in it and mingles with it, just as it directly experiences by the senses what is connected to them. Then the brightness of it mixes with the hearts, and *ḥaqq al-yaqīn* remains for them. This is the highest level of faith, which is the state of *ṣiddīqiyyah* (truthfulness), in which the ranks of believers differ.

Some scholars gave an example for the three degrees. He said: If someone whose truthfulness you are certain of tells you, "I have honey, and I want to feed you some of it," and you believe him, that is *ʿilm al-yaqīn*. When he brings it before you, that is *ʿayn al-yaqīn*. When you taste it, that is *ḥaqq al-yaqīn*.

On this basis, this annexation is not of the type of a qualified noun to its quality, but rather of the type of annexing a genus to its species. *ʿIlm*, *ʿayn* and *ḥaqq* are more general than being certainty, so the general is annexed to the specific, like "some of the goods" and "all the dirhams." Since the annexing word and the annexed word in this construction both refer to one and the same entity, unlike your saying "the house of ʿAmr" or "the garment of Zayd," those who thought it was annexing a qualified noun to its quality were mistaken. Rather, it is of the type of annexing a genus to its species, like "a garment of silk" and "a ring of silver." The annexed term may be different from the annexing term, so they do not refer to one entity; or it may be homogeneous with it, so they refer to one named thing. And Allah knows best.

Then He concluded the surah with His saying: ﴿So glorify the name of your Lord, the Mighty﴾.

It is fitting for this conclusion, because it contains information about the greatness and majesty of the Lord, the mention of the immensity of His dominion, the operation of His judgment with justice over His servants in this world and the Hereafter, and the mention of His greatness in sending His Messenger and sending down His Book. He is greater, more glorious and more magnificent in the eyes of the people of His heavens and the believers among His servants than to approve a lie attributed to Him and fabricated against Him, one that alters His religion, abrogates His laws, kills His servants, and reports about Him what has no reality. Yet He, glorified is He, supports and aids him, answers his supplications, seizes his enemies, raises his station and exalts his remembrance. He is the Mighty, whose greatness refuses to do such a thing to one who comes with the vilest kinds of lying and wrongdoing. So glorified is our Lord, the Mighty, and exalted far above what the ignorant attribute to Him, a great exaltation.

That is, if he had brought something of his own accord, We would have seized him by the right hand, cut the aorta of his heart, and destroyed him. God has protected him from inclining toward his enemies even by a particle of his heart, and from fabricating speech against Him, glory be to Him. How many have inclined toward his enemies and fabricated speech against Him from their own selves, and He gave them respite and paid them no heed, like all the people of innovation (ahl al-bid'ah, those who introduce novelties into religion), who fabricate against His names, attributes, and religion.

He also said in *al-Madarij* (*Madarij al-Salikin*):

When you contemplate the Qur'an, you see it calling out to this, displaying it and repeating it for those who have understanding and a heart that is attentive to God. God, exalted is He, said: ﴿And if he had fabricated against Us some sayings, We would have seized him by the right hand, then We would have cut from him the aorta, and none of you could have held Us off from him.﴾

Do you not see how He, glory be to Him, informs us that His perfection, His wisdom, and His power refuse to let stand one who fabricates some sayings against Him? Rather, He must make him an example to His servants, as His sunnah has run concerning those who fabricate against Him.

He also said in *al-Tibyan fi Aqsam al-Qur'an* (*al-Tibyan*):

Then, glory be to Him, He established a decisive proof of the truthfulness of His Messenger, and that he did not fabricate against Him in what he said, and that if he had fabricated against Him, He would not have approved it and would have hastened his destruction. For the perfection of His knowledge, power, and wisdom refuses to let stand one who fabricates against Him, forges lies about Him, leads His servants astray, permits the blood of those who denied him, their honor, and their property, spreads corruption, tyranny, and falsehood on earth, and opposes creation. How then could it befit the Wisest of the wise, the Most Merciful of the merciful, and the Most Capable of the capable to let him stand in this? Rather, how could it befit Him to support him, help him, exalt him, make him prevail, and grant him victory over the people of truth, while he sheds their blood, permits their property, their children, and their women, saying: "God commanded me to do this and permitted it to me"? Rather, how could it befit Him to confirm him with every kind of confirmation: confirming him by approving him, by the signs that necessarily imply his truthfulness, whose indication of confirmation is like the indication of confirmation by speech, which is manifest. Then He confirms him by all their kinds in their variety, so that each sign on its own confirms him, and then through the combination of those signs there arises a confirmation above the confirmation of each sign individually. Then creation is unable to oppose him. Then He confirms him by His speech and His word, then establishes the decisive proof that this is His word and His speech, bearing witness to him by His approval, His action, and His word. It is therefore among the greatest impossibilities, the most false of falsehoods, and the clearest of slander, that the Wisest of the wise and Lord of the worlds should permit such a thing to be done to the liar who fabricates against Him, who is the worst of creation absolutely. Whoever permits God to do this to the worst and most lying of His creatures has certainly not believed in God, nor known God, and this is not the Lord of the worlds. It is not fitting to attribute this to anyone who has a grain of intellect, wisdom, and reason. Whoever does this has disgraced himself and proclaimed his own ignorance.

I recall a debate that took place between me and some Jews. After I had argued at length for the prophethood of the Prophet, I said to him: "Denying his prophethood entails disparaging the Lord of the worlds and belittling Him in the most abominable way." He said: "How can you say such a thing?" I said: "Its explanation is up to me. Now listen: you claim that he was not a messenger, but rather a dominant king who subdued people by his sword until they submitted to him. He remained for twenty-three years lying against God, saying, 'It was revealed to me,' when nothing had been revealed to him; 'He commanded me,' when He had not commanded him; 'He forbade me,' when He had not forbidden him; and he said, 'God said such-and-such,' when He had not said it; and he made lawful such-and-such, forbade such-and-such, made obligatory such-and-such, and made reprehensible such-and-such, when He had not made any of these lawful, forbidden, obligatory, or reprehensible. Rather, he did all of that of his own accord, lying and fabricating against God, and against His prophets, His messengers, and His angels. Then he remained for thirteen years after that, going about among His servants, shedding their blood, seizing their property, enslaving their women and children, though they had committed no offense except rejecting him and opposing him, and in all of this he kept saying, 'God commanded me to do this,' when He had not commanded him. Moreover, he strove to change the religions of the messengers, abrogate their laws, and dissolve their sacred ordinances. This is his condition according to you. Then either the Lord, exalted is He, knew of all this and was informed of his condition, seeing it and witnessing it, or He did not. If you say that all of this was hidden from God, unknown to Him, then you have attributed to the Lord, exalted is He, an extreme ignorance, for He did not become aware of this tremendous event, nor know it, nor see it. If you say rather that it happened with His knowledge, His awareness, and His witnessing, it is said to you: was He able to change that, to seize his hand and to come between him and it, or not? If you say He was not able to do so, then you attribute to Him an incapacity that contradicts lordship, and this man and his followers would have been more capable than He of carrying out their will. If you say rather that He was able, but He empowered him, supported him, and gave him dominion over creation, and did not help His friends and the followers of His messengers, then you attribute to Him the greatest folly, injustice, and failure to uphold wisdom. This would hold even if He had merely left him free to do what he did; how much more so when, in all of that, He is his helper and supporter, answers his supplications, destroys those who opposed and denied him, confirms him in every kind of confirmation, and manifests signs through his hands, which if all the people of the earth gathered to produce one of them, they could not, and they would be unable to do so."

And every moment there happens to him, from the causes of victory, empowerment, manifestation, exaltation, and the multiplication of followers, something beyond the ordinary. Thus it becomes clear that whoever denies that he was a messenger and a prophet has blamed God, disparaged Him, and attributed to Him ignorance, incapacity, and folly.

I said to him: "This is not undermined by the tyrannical kings whom God empowered on earth for a time, and then cut off their root, nullified their sunnah, and erased their traces and their oppression. For those did not bring anything of this kind, nor were they supported and helped, nor did signs appear at their hands, nor did the Lord, exalted is He, confirm them by His approval, by His action, or by His word. Rather, their command was the opposite of the Messenger's command, like Pharaoh, Nimrod, and their likes. Nor is this undermined by those who claimed prophethood among the liars, for their condition was the opposite of the Messenger's condition in every respect. Rather, their condition is among the clearest proofs of the Messenger's truthfulness. Among God's wisdom, glory be to Him, is that He brought such people into existence so that the condition of the liars and the condition of the truthful might be known, and their appearance was among the clearest evidences for the truthfulness of the messengers. The difference between these and those is shown by their opposites, and things are made clear by their opposites. Thus knowledge of the proofs of falsehood and its confusions is among the kinds of proofs of truth and its demonstrations."

When he heard this, he said: "God forbid! We do not say that he was a tyrannical king, but a noble prophet, and whoever follows him is among the happy. Likewise, whoever follows Moses is like one who follows Muhammad."

I said to him: "Everything you disguise by this is null. For if you acknowledge that he is a truthful prophet, then it is necessary to affirm him in everything he reported. His followers and his enemies alike know by necessity that he called all people to faith, and informed that whoever does not believe in him is an unbeliever destined for the Fire, and that he fought those of the People of the Book who did not believe in him, branded them with disbelief, and permitted their property, their blood, their women, and their children. If that was an aggression and an injustice on his part, then he was not a prophet, and the matter returns to disparagement of the Lord, exalted is He. If that was by God's command and His revelation, then no one may oppose him, abandon his followers, and it is binding to affirm him in what he reported and obey him in what he commanded."

Glory be to Him has pointed to this kingship in more than one place in His Book. He said: ﴿And if he had fabricated against Us some sayings, We would have seized him by the right hand, then We would have cut from him the aorta, and none of you could have held Us off from him.﴾

He, glory be to Him, says: If he had fabricated against Us a single saying of his own accord, which We did not say and did not reveal to him, We would not have let it stand; We would have seized him by his right hand and then destroyed him. This is one of the two opinions. Ibn Qutaybah said: there are two opinions on this. One is that "the right hand" means strength and power, and the right hand is used in place of strength, because the strength of everything is in its right side. I say: according to this, "the right hand" is a description of the seizing, and this is the view of Ibn Abbas regarding "the right hand."

He said: The lexicographers have another interpretation of this. It is that the speech follows what people are accustomed to, namely taking a man by the hand when they want to punish him. They say, when they wish to punish a man, "Take his hand," and the sultan and the judge most often say this after the verdict has become due: "Take his hand, seize his hand." So it is as if He said: If he had lied against Us in anything that was conveyed to you from Us, We would have seized him by the right hand, then punished him by cutting the aorta. This is the meaning that al-Hasan adopted.

Thus He informed, glory be to Him, that if he had fabricated any saying against Him, He would not have let it stand and would have hastened the punishment. For lying against God is not like lying against anyone else, and it is not fitting for Him to let the one who lies against Him stand, let alone to help him, support him, and confirm him.

And by His saying: ﴿Then We would have cut from him the aorta﴾.

The watin is the aorta of the heart, a vein that runs along the spine until it connects to the heart. If it is severed, the powers fail and its owner dies. This is the statement of all the lexicographers. Ibn Qutaybah said: He did not mean that We would cut that very vein, but He meant that if he lied against Us, We would have stopped him or killed him, so it is as if he had been cut at the aorta. He said: Something similar is His saying (of the Prophet), "The poison of Khaybar kept recurring to me, and now is the time my abhar was severed." The abhar is a vein connected to the heart; when it is severed, its owner dies. So it is as if he said: Now the poison has killed me, and I was like one whose abhar had been severed.

Then He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And none of you could have held Us off from him.﴾

That is, no one could keep him away from Me or prevent him from Me.

The second passage is His saying: ﴿Or do they say, "He has fabricated against God a lie"? If God willed, He would seal upon your heart, and God would erase falsehood and establish truth by His words. Indeed, He is Knower of what is within the breasts.﴾

Regarding the meaning of this verse, people have two opinions. One is the view of Mujahid and Muqatil: "If God willed, He would bind your heart with patience against their harm so that it would not weigh on you." The second is the view of Qatadah: "If God willed, He would make you forget the Qur'an and cut off revelation from you." This second view is weaker than the first, for several reasons.

First, this was given as an answer to them and as a denial of their claim that Muhammad lied against God and fabricated this Qur'an against Him. So He answered them with the best answer, which is that God, the Exalted, is capable and nothing can overpower Him. If it were as you say, He would have sealed his heart, so that he could not produce anything of it; rather the heart would become like a sealed thing, so that nothing reaches what is in it. The meaning returns to this: if he had fabricated against Me, I would not have enabled him or let him stand. And it is evident that such speech does not issue from a heart that has been sealed. For in it are the knowledge of the first and the last, the knowledge of the origin and the return, the world and the Hereafter, the knowledge that none knows but God, the complete clarity, eloquence, grandeur, and majesty, and the reports of the unseen, none of which the one whose heart was sealed could produce, nor any part of it. Had I not sent it down upon your heart and made it easy on your tongue, he could not have brought you anything of it. How is this related to the meaning that the others mentioned? How does it fit with the report of their saying, and how does it contain a refutation of them?

Second, mere binding of the heart with patience against their harm is found in both the truthful and the falsehood-speaker, so it does not indicate distinguishing between them, nor is it a refutation of their saying. For patience under the harm of one who denies does not by itself indicate the truthfulness of the one who reports.

Third, the one who binds the heart of a servant is not said to have sealed his heart, and this is not recognized in the usage of the addressees, nor in the language of the Arabs, nor is it what is customary in the Qur'an. Rather, the customary use of sealing the heart in the Qur'an, in every instance of the expression, concerns the unbelievers, as in His saying: ﴿God has sealed upon their hearts﴾, and His saying: ﴿Have you seen him who takes his own desire as his god, and God misguides him knowingly, and seals his hearing and his heart, and places over his sight a covering?﴾ and its counterparts.

As for binding the heart of a servant with patience, it is like His saying: ﴿And We bound their hearts when they stood up and said, "Our Lord is the Lord of the heavens and the earth."﴾ And His saying: ﴿And the heart of Moses' mother became empty; she was about to reveal it, had We not bound her heart.﴾ A person may say in supplication, "O God, bind my heart," and it is not fitting for him to say, "O God, seal my heart."

Fourth, when He, glory be to Him, recounts their sayings that he fabricated it, He does not answer them with this answer. Rather, He answers them that if he had fabricated it, they would not have been able to possess anything for him from God, but He would have seized him and they could not have rescued him. Like His saying: ﴿Or do they say, "He has fabricated it"? Say: If I had fabricated it, you could not possess for me anything from God.﴾ And at other times He answers them by challenging them to produce its like or a part of it, and at other times by establishing decisive proofs that it is the truth and that they are the liars and fabricators. This is what is fitting as an answer to this question, not merely patience.

Fifth, this verse is a parallel to what we are discussing: that if He willed, He would not have let him stand and would not have empowered him. And the interpretation of the Qur'an by the Qur'an is among the most eloquent forms of exegesis.

Sixth, there is no indication in the context of the verse of patience in any way, neither by correspondence, nor by inclusion, nor by implication. So how is it known that He intended this meaning, when this meaning does not recur elsewhere to be taken as its sense, unlike the meaning that He would come between him and it and not enable him to fabricate against Him? He has mentioned this in several places.

Seventh, He, glory be to Him, informed that if He willed, He would not have recited it to them nor made them aware of it, and that this is only by His will, permission, and knowledge, as He, the Exalted, said: ﴿Say: If God had willed, I would not have recited it to you, nor would He have made you aware of it.﴾

This is among the most eloquent and manifest arguments. That is: this speech is not from me, nor of my own making, and I cannot fabricate it against God. Had that been within my capacity, it would have been within the capacity of one who has knowledge, writing, mixing with people, and learning from them. But God sent me with it. Had He willed, He would not have sent it down or made it easy upon my tongue; He would not have let me recite it to you or inform you of it at all, neither on my tongue nor on the tongue of anyone else. Rather, He revealed it to me and permitted me to recite it to you and make you aware of it after you had not been aware of it. So had it been a lie and a fabrication, as you say, it would have been possible for someone other than me to recite it to you and for you to become aware of it through him, for lying is not beyond human capacity. Yet you were not aware of this and did not hear it except from me, and you did not hear it from any human other than me.

Then He answered an implied question: that he had learned it from someone else or had fabricated it of his own accord. He said: ﴿So I had remained among you a lifetime before it.﴾ You know my condition, and my journeys, my comings and goings, my truthfulness and my trustworthiness are not hidden from you. For this reason I was never able to say anything of it at all, nor had any knowledge of it or of any part of it. Then I brought it to you suddenly, without effort, without learning, and without the means by which I could have acquired it or any part of it. This is among the clearest evidences and most manifest proofs that it is from God; He revealed it to me and sent it down upon me. Had He willed, He would not have done so: He would not have enabled me to recite it, nor enabled you to know it. Rather, He enabled me to recite it and enabled you to know it, so you did not know it nor any part of it, and before it was revealed to me I was not reciting it nor any part of it. So consider the soundness of this proof, the excellence of its composition, and the clarity of its indication.

From this is His, glory be to Him, saying: ﴿And if We willed, We would surely take away what We revealed to you; then you would not find for yourself any guardian against Us in respect to it.﴾

This is the fitting one to match His saying: ﴿Or do they say, "He has fabricated against God a lie"? If God willed, He would seal upon your heart,﴾ and His saying: ﴿And if he had fabricated against Us some sayings, We would have seized him by the right hand.﴾ And it is an independent proof mentioned in the Qur'an in several ways. And God knows best.

Eighth, such a construction in the Qur'an comes only for negation, not for affirmation, as in His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And if We willed, We would surely take away what We revealed to you.﴾ And His saying: ﴿If He wills, He will take you away, O people, and bring others.﴾ And His saying: ﴿If He wills, He will still the wind, and they would remain motionless on its back.﴾ And His saying: ﴿If We will, We will cause the earth to swallow them, or drop upon them a piece of the sky.﴾ And its counterparts. It has come only where what follows the verb of will is negated.

The ninth point: sealing the heart does not necessitate patience. Rather, a servant's heart may be sealed and his patience taken from him. Indeed, when the heart is sealed, patience disappears and weakens. This differs from binding (rabt) upon the heart, which does necessitate patience, as Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And He sends down upon you water from the sky to purify you by it, remove from you the defilement of Satan, and strengthen your hearts﴾. In the language, rabt means tying or binding, and so it is said of anyone who endures a matter that he "bound his heart," as if he restrained his heart from agitation. From this comes the expression "he is steadfast of heart" (rabit al-jash).

Al-Wahidi thought that (ʿalā) is superfluous, and that the meaning is "He binds your hearts." That is not what he supposed. There is a clear difference between binding a thing and binding upon it. One says rabata al-faras and al-dabbah (he tied the horse and the animal), and one does not say rabata ʿalayha. When the binding surrounds and covers a thing, it is said rabata ʿalayhi, as if he had encompassed it with the binding. Therefore it is said rabata ʿalā qalbihi, which is more eloquent than saying rabata qalbahu. The point is that with this binding comes stronger and more enduring patience, unlike sealing.

The tenth point: sealing (khatm) is the fastening of the heart so that it does not perceive or understand. It is a barrier preventing knowledge and intention. The Prophet (ﷺ) knew the words of his enemies that he had fabricated the Qur'an, and he perceived them. Allah did not place upon his heart a barrier preventing him from perceiving that or knowing it.

If it is said that the matter is so, but that Allah placed upon his heart a barrier preventing harm from their words, this is more fitting to be called a sealing. Their words did harm him and grieved them, as Allah the Exalted says: ﴿We know that what they say grieves you﴾. The arrival of this harm to him was from Allah's honour toward him, for no prophet was harmed as he was harmed. The interpretation of the verse is the view of Qatadah, and Allah knows best.

Then Allah the Exalted informed that the Qur'an is a reminder (tadhkirah) for the God-fearing (muttaqin), by which the God-fearing one is reminded, sees what benefits him so that he pursues it, and what harms him so that he avoids it. By it he is reminded of the names, attributes and actions of the Lord, so that he believes. By it he is reminded of His reward and punishment, His threat and command, His prohibition, and His signs in His friends and His enemies, in himself, and in what purifies, cleanses and elevates it, and in what corrupts, conceals and debases it. By it he is reminded of the knowledge of origin and return, of Paradise and Hellfire, and of the knowledge of good and evil. It is therefore the reminder in reality, a proof for the worlds and a benefit and guidance for those who seek knowledge.

Then He, glorified is He, said: ﴿And indeed We know that among you are deniers﴾, meaning: they are not hidden from Us, and We will repay them for their denial.

Then Allah the Exalted informed that His Messenger and His speech are a cause of anguish (hasrah) for the disbelievers when they witness the reality of what he reported. Their denial will be among the greatest of their regrets, when regret will no longer benefit them. Thus is every one who denies the truth and affirms falsehood: when the reality of what he denied and affirmed is revealed to him, his denial and affirmation become a regret for him, like one who neglected what would benefit him at the time of acquiring it, until his need for it becomes intense and he witnesses the success of those who attained it, and his neglect becomes a regret upon him.

Then Allah the Exalted informed that the Qur'an and the Messenger are *ḥaqq al-yaqīn* (the sure truth of certainty). It is said that this is of the type of annexing a qualified noun to its quality, meaning "the true certainty," like *masjid al-jāmiʿ* and *ṣalāt al-ūlā*. This point requires verification, so we say, and with Allah is success.

(Section)

Allah the Exalted mentioned in His Book the degrees of certainty (yaqin), and they are three: *ḥaqq al-yaqīn* (the truth of certainty), *ʿilm al-yaqīn* (the knowledge of certainty), and *ʿayn al-yaqīn* (the eye of certainty), as Allah the Exalted says: ﴿No! If you knew with the knowledge of certainty, you would surely see the Hellfire; then you would surely see it with the eye of certainty﴾. These are three degrees of certainty. The first is its knowledge, which is complete affirmation without any doubt or uncertainty that undermines that affirmation, such as the knowledge of certainty about Paradise, for example, and their certainty that it is the abode of the God-fearing and the dwelling of the believers. This is the level of knowledge, like their certainty that the messengers reported it from Allah, and their certainty of the truthfulness of the one who reports.

The second degree is *ʿayn al-yaqīn*, which is the level of seeing and witnessing, as Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Then you would surely see it with the eye of certainty﴾. Between this degree and the one before it there is the difference between knowledge and witnessing: certainty belongs to hearing, and the eye of certainty belongs to sight. In the Musnad of Imam Ahmad, it is related from the Prophet (ﷺ) as a marfūʿ report: "The report is not like one who witnesses it." This is the degree which Abraham the Friend (al-Khalil) asked his Lord to show him, how He gives life to the dead, so that he might attain, alongside knowledge of certainty, the eye of certainty. His request was an increase for himself and a reassurance for his heart, so that the heart is at rest at the moment of witnessing and is content by closing the distance between report and seeing. It is upon this distance that the Prophet used the word "doubt," when he said: "We have more right to doubt than Abraham." Far be it that there was any doubt, either in Abraham or in anyone else. Rather, it is the eye after knowledge, witnessing after report, and sight after hearing.

The third degree is *ḥaqq al-yaqīn*, which is direct contact with a thing through perception of it, as when they enter Paradise and enjoy what is in it. In this world they are at the level of *ʿilm al-yaqīn*; on the Day of Standing, as they draw near and are brought close until they witness it, they are at the level of *ʿayn al-yaqīn*; and when they enter it and experience its bliss, they are at the level of *ḥaqq al-yaqīn*. Direct contact with the known object sometimes occurs through the outward senses and sometimes through the heart. Therefore Allah says: ﴿And indeed, it is the truth of certainty﴾. The heart directly experiences faith in it and mingles with it, just as it directly experiences by the senses what is connected to them. Then the brightness of it mixes with the hearts, and *ḥaqq al-yaqīn* remains for them. This is the highest level of faith, which is the state of *ṣiddīqiyyah* (truthfulness), in which the ranks of believers differ.

Some scholars gave an example for the three degrees. He said: If someone whose truthfulness you are certain of tells you, "I have honey, and I want to feed you some of it," and you believe him, that is *ʿilm al-yaqīn*. When he brings it before you, that is *ʿayn al-yaqīn*. When you taste it, that is *ḥaqq al-yaqīn*.

On this basis, this annexation is not of the type of a qualified noun to its quality, but rather of the type of annexing a genus to its species. *ʿIlm*, *ʿayn* and *ḥaqq* are more general than being certainty, so the general is annexed to the specific, like "some of the goods" and "all the dirhams." Since the annexing word and the annexed word in this construction both refer to one and the same entity, unlike your saying "the house of ʿAmr" or "the garment of Zayd," those who thought it was annexing a qualified noun to its quality were mistaken. Rather, it is of the type of annexing a genus to its species, like "a garment of silk" and "a ring of silver." The annexed term may be different from the annexing term, so they do not refer to one entity; or it may be homogeneous with it, so they refer to one named thing. And Allah knows best.

Then He concluded the surah with His saying: ﴿So glorify the name of your Lord, the Mighty﴾.

It is fitting for this conclusion, because it contains information about the greatness and majesty of the Lord, the mention of the immensity of His dominion, the operation of His judgment with justice over His servants in this world and the Hereafter, and the mention of His greatness in sending His Messenger and sending down His Book. He is greater, more glorious and more magnificent in the eyes of the people of His heavens and the believers among His servants than to approve a lie attributed to Him and fabricated against Him, one that alters His religion, abrogates His laws, kills His servants, and reports about Him what has no reality. Yet He, glorified is He, supports and aids him, answers his supplications, seizes his enemies, raises his station and exalts his remembrance. He is the Mighty, whose greatness refuses to do such a thing to one who comes with the vilest kinds of lying and wrongdoing. So glorified is our Lord, the Mighty, and exalted far above what the ignorant attribute to Him, a great exaltation.

That is, if he had brought something of his own accord, We would have seized him by the right hand, cut the aorta of his heart, and destroyed him. God has protected him from inclining toward his enemies even by a particle of his heart, and from fabricating speech against Him, glory be to Him. How many have inclined toward his enemies and fabricated speech against Him from their own selves, and He gave them respite and paid them no heed, like all the people of innovation (ahl al-bid'ah, those who introduce novelties into religion), who fabricate against His names, attributes, and religion.

He also said in *al-Madarij* (*Madarij al-Salikin*):

When you contemplate the Qur'an, you see it calling out to this, displaying it and repeating it for those who have understanding and a heart that is attentive to God. God, exalted is He, said: ﴿And if he had fabricated against Us some sayings, We would have seized him by the right hand, then We would have cut from him the aorta, and none of you could have held Us off from him.﴾

Do you not see how He, glory be to Him, informs us that His perfection, His wisdom, and His power refuse to let stand one who fabricates some sayings against Him? Rather, He must make him an example to His servants, as His sunnah has run concerning those who fabricate against Him.

He also said in *al-Tibyan fi Aqsam al-Qur'an* (*al-Tibyan*):

Then, glory be to Him, He established a decisive proof of the truthfulness of His Messenger, and that he did not fabricate against Him in what he said, and that if he had fabricated against Him, He would not have approved it and would have hastened his destruction. For the perfection of His knowledge, power, and wisdom refuses to let stand one who fabricates against Him, forges lies about Him, leads His servants astray, permits the blood of those who denied him, their honor, and their property, spreads corruption, tyranny, and falsehood on earth, and opposes creation. How then could it befit the Wisest of the wise, the Most Merciful of the merciful, and the Most Capable of the capable to let him stand in this? Rather, how could it befit Him to support him, help him, exalt him, make him prevail, and grant him victory over the people of truth, while he sheds their blood, permits their property, their children, and their women, saying: "God commanded me to do this and permitted it to me"? Rather, how could it befit Him to confirm him with every kind of confirmation: confirming him by approving him, by the signs that necessarily imply his truthfulness, whose indication of confirmation is like the indication of confirmation by speech, which is manifest. Then He confirms him by all their kinds in their variety, so that each sign on its own confirms him, and then through the combination of those signs there arises a confirmation above the confirmation of each sign individually. Then creation is unable to oppose him. Then He confirms him by His speech and His word, then establishes the decisive proof that this is His word and His speech, bearing witness to him by His approval, His action, and His word. It is therefore among the greatest impossibilities, the most false of falsehoods, and the clearest of slander, that the Wisest of the wise and Lord of the worlds should permit such a thing to be done to the liar who fabricates against Him, who is the worst of creation absolutely. Whoever permits God to do this to the worst and most lying of His creatures has certainly not believed in God, nor known God, and this is not the Lord of the worlds. It is not fitting to attribute this to anyone who has a grain of intellect, wisdom, and reason. Whoever does this has disgraced himself and proclaimed his own ignorance.

I recall a debate that took place between me and some Jews. After I had argued at length for the prophethood of the Prophet, I said to him: "Denying his prophethood entails disparaging the Lord of the worlds and belittling Him in the most abominable way." He said: "How can you say such a thing?" I said: "Its explanation is up to me. Now listen: you claim that he was not a messenger, but rather a dominant king who subdued people by his sword until they submitted to him. He remained for twenty-three years lying against God, saying, 'It was revealed to me,' when nothing had been revealed to him; 'He commanded me,' when He had not commanded him; 'He forbade me,' when He had not forbidden him; and he said, 'God said such-and-such,' when He had not said it; and he made lawful such-and-such, forbade such-and-such, made obligatory such-and-such, and made reprehensible such-and-such, when He had not made any of these lawful, forbidden, obligatory, or reprehensible. Rather, he did all of that of his own accord, lying and fabricating against God, and against His prophets, His messengers, and His angels. Then he remained for thirteen years after that, going about among His servants, shedding their blood, seizing their property, enslaving their women and children, though they had committed no offense except rejecting him and opposing him, and in all of this he kept saying, 'God commanded me to do this,' when He had not commanded him. Moreover, he strove to change the religions of the messengers, abrogate their laws, and dissolve their sacred ordinances. This is his condition according to you. Then either the Lord, exalted is He, knew of all this and was informed of his condition, seeing it and witnessing it, or He did not. If you say that all of this was hidden from God, unknown to Him, then you have attributed to the Lord, exalted is He, an extreme ignorance, for He did not become aware of this tremendous event, nor know it, nor see it. If you say rather that it happened with His knowledge, His awareness, and His witnessing, it is said to you: was He able to change that, to seize his hand and to come between him and it, or not? If you say He was not able to do so, then you attribute to Him an incapacity that contradicts lordship, and this man and his followers would have been more capable than He of carrying out their will. If you say rather that He was able, but He empowered him, supported him, and gave him dominion over creation, and did not help His friends and the followers of His messengers, then you attribute to Him the greatest folly, injustice, and failure to uphold wisdom. This would hold even if He had merely left him free to do what he did; how much more so when, in all of that, He is his helper and supporter, answers his supplications, destroys those who opposed and denied him, confirms him in every kind of confirmation, and manifests signs through his hands, which if all the people of the earth gathered to produce one of them, they could not, and they would be unable to do so."

And every moment there happens to him, from the causes of victory, empowerment, manifestation, exaltation, and the multiplication of followers, something beyond the ordinary. Thus it becomes clear that whoever denies that he was a messenger and a prophet has blamed God, disparaged Him, and attributed to Him ignorance, incapacity, and folly.

I said to him: "This is not undermined by the tyrannical kings whom God empowered on earth for a time, and then cut off their root, nullified their sunnah, and erased their traces and their oppression. For those did not bring anything of this kind, nor were they supported and helped, nor did signs appear at their hands, nor did the Lord, exalted is He, confirm them by His approval, by His action, or by His word. Rather, their command was the opposite of the Messenger's command, like Pharaoh, Nimrod, and their likes. Nor is this undermined by those who claimed prophethood among the liars, for their condition was the opposite of the Messenger's condition in every respect. Rather, their condition is among the clearest proofs of the Messenger's truthfulness. Among God's wisdom, glory be to Him, is that He brought such people into existence so that the condition of the liars and the condition of the truthful might be known, and their appearance was among the clearest evidences for the truthfulness of the messengers. The difference between these and those is shown by their opposites, and things are made clear by their opposites. Thus knowledge of the proofs of falsehood and its confusions is among the kinds of proofs of truth and its demonstrations."

When he heard this, he said: "God forbid! We do not say that he was a tyrannical king, but a noble prophet, and whoever follows him is among the happy. Likewise, whoever follows Moses is like one who follows Muhammad."

I said to him: "Everything you disguise by this is null. For if you acknowledge that he is a truthful prophet, then it is necessary to affirm him in everything he reported. His followers and his enemies alike know by necessity that he called all people to faith, and informed that whoever does not believe in him is an unbeliever destined for the Fire, and that he fought those of the People of the Book who did not believe in him, branded them with disbelief, and permitted their property, their blood, their women, and their children. If that was an aggression and an injustice on his part, then he was not a prophet, and the matter returns to disparagement of the Lord, exalted is He. If that was by God's command and His revelation, then no one may oppose him, abandon his followers, and it is binding to affirm him in what he reported and obey him in what he commanded."

Glory be to Him has pointed to this kingship in more than one place in His Book. He said: ﴿And if he had fabricated against Us some sayings, We would have seized him by the right hand, then We would have cut from him the aorta, and none of you could have held Us off from him.﴾

He, glory be to Him, says: If he had fabricated against Us a single saying of his own accord, which We did not say and did not reveal to him, We would not have let it stand; We would have seized him by his right hand and then destroyed him. This is one of the two opinions. Ibn Qutaybah said: there are two opinions on this. One is that "the right hand" means strength and power, and the right hand is used in place of strength, because the strength of everything is in its right side. I say: according to this, "the right hand" is a description of the seizing, and this is the view of Ibn Abbas regarding "the right hand."

He said: The lexicographers have another interpretation of this. It is that the speech follows what people are accustomed to, namely taking a man by the hand when they want to punish him. They say, when they wish to punish a man, "Take his hand," and the sultan and the judge most often say this after the verdict has become due: "Take his hand, seize his hand." So it is as if He said: If he had lied against Us in anything that was conveyed to you from Us, We would have seized him by the right hand, then punished him by cutting the aorta. This is the meaning that al-Hasan adopted.

Thus He informed, glory be to Him, that if he had fabricated any saying against Him, He would not have let it stand and would have hastened the punishment. For lying against God is not like lying against anyone else, and it is not fitting for Him to let the one who lies against Him stand, let alone to help him, support him, and confirm him.

And by His saying: ﴿Then We would have cut from him the aorta﴾.

The watin is the aorta of the heart, a vein that runs along the spine until it connects to the heart. If it is severed, the powers fail and its owner dies. This is the statement of all the lexicographers. Ibn Qutaybah said: He did not mean that We would cut that very vein, but He meant that if he lied against Us, We would have stopped him or killed him, so it is as if he had been cut at the aorta. He said: Something similar is His saying (of the Prophet), "The poison of Khaybar kept recurring to me, and now is the time my abhar was severed." The abhar is a vein connected to the heart; when it is severed, its owner dies. So it is as if he said: Now the poison has killed me, and I was like one whose abhar had been severed.

Then He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And none of you could have held Us off from him.﴾

That is, no one could keep him away from Me or prevent him from Me.

The second passage is His saying: ﴿Or do they say, "He has fabricated against God a lie"? If God willed, He would seal upon your heart, and God would erase falsehood and establish truth by His words. Indeed, He is Knower of what is within the breasts.﴾

Regarding the meaning of this verse, people have two opinions. One is the view of Mujahid and Muqatil: "If God willed, He would bind your heart with patience against their harm so that it would not weigh on you." The second is the view of Qatadah: "If God willed, He would make you forget the Qur'an and cut off revelation from you." This second view is weaker than the first, for several reasons.

First, this was given as an answer to them and as a denial of their claim that Muhammad lied against God and fabricated this Qur'an against Him. So He answered them with the best answer, which is that God, the Exalted, is capable and nothing can overpower Him. If it were as you say, He would have sealed his heart, so that he could not produce anything of it; rather the heart would become like a sealed thing, so that nothing reaches what is in it. The meaning returns to this: if he had fabricated against Me, I would not have enabled him or let him stand. And it is evident that such speech does not issue from a heart that has been sealed. For in it are the knowledge of the first and the last, the knowledge of the origin and the return, the world and the Hereafter, the knowledge that none knows but God, the complete clarity, eloquence, grandeur, and majesty, and the reports of the unseen, none of which the one whose heart was sealed could produce, nor any part of it. Had I not sent it down upon your heart and made it easy on your tongue, he could not have brought you anything of it. How is this related to the meaning that the others mentioned? How does it fit with the report of their saying, and how does it contain a refutation of them?

Second, mere binding of the heart with patience against their harm is found in both the truthful and the falsehood-speaker, so it does not indicate distinguishing between them, nor is it a refutation of their saying. For patience under the harm of one who denies does not by itself indicate the truthfulness of the one who reports.

Third, the one who binds the heart of a servant is not said to have sealed his heart, and this is not recognized in the usage of the addressees, nor in the language of the Arabs, nor is it what is customary in the Qur'an. Rather, the customary use of sealing the heart in the Qur'an, in every instance of the expression, concerns the unbelievers, as in His saying: ﴿God has sealed upon their hearts﴾, and His saying: ﴿Have you seen him who takes his own desire as his god, and God misguides him knowingly, and seals his hearing and his heart, and places over his sight a covering?﴾ and its counterparts.

As for binding the heart of a servant with patience, it is like His saying: ﴿And We bound their hearts when they stood up and said, "Our Lord is the Lord of the heavens and the earth."﴾ And His saying: ﴿And the heart of Moses' mother became empty; she was about to reveal it, had We not bound her heart.﴾ A person may say in supplication, "O God, bind my heart," and it is not fitting for him to say, "O God, seal my heart."

Fourth, when He, glory be to Him, recounts their sayings that he fabricated it, He does not answer them with this answer. Rather, He answers them that if he had fabricated it, they would not have been able to possess anything for him from God, but He would have seized him and they could not have rescued him. Like His saying: ﴿Or do they say, "He has fabricated it"? Say: If I had fabricated it, you could not possess for me anything from God.﴾ And at other times He answers them by challenging them to produce its like or a part of it, and at other times by establishing decisive proofs that it is the truth and that they are the liars and fabricators. This is what is fitting as an answer to this question, not merely patience.

Fifth, this verse is a parallel to what we are discussing: that if He willed, He would not have let him stand and would not have empowered him. And the interpretation of the Qur'an by the Qur'an is among the most eloquent forms of exegesis.

Sixth, there is no indication in the context of the verse of patience in any way, neither by correspondence, nor by inclusion, nor by implication. So how is it known that He intended this meaning, when this meaning does not recur elsewhere to be taken as its sense, unlike the meaning that He would come between him and it and not enable him to fabricate against Him? He has mentioned this in several places.

Seventh, He, glory be to Him, informed that if He willed, He would not have recited it to them nor made them aware of it, and that this is only by His will, permission, and knowledge, as He, the Exalted, said: ﴿Say: If God had willed, I would not have recited it to you, nor would He have made you aware of it.﴾

This is among the most eloquent and manifest arguments. That is: this speech is not from me, nor of my own making, and I cannot fabricate it against God. Had that been within my capacity, it would have been within the capacity of one who has knowledge, writing, mixing with people, and learning from them. But God sent me with it. Had He willed, He would not have sent it down or made it easy upon my tongue; He would not have let me recite it to you or inform you of it at all, neither on my tongue nor on the tongue of anyone else. Rather, He revealed it to me and permitted me to recite it to you and make you aware of it after you had not been aware of it. So had it been a lie and a fabrication, as you say, it would have been possible for someone other than me to recite it to you and for you to become aware of it through him, for lying is not beyond human capacity. Yet you were not aware of this and did not hear it except from me, and you did not hear it from any human other than me.

Then He answered an implied question: that he had learned it from someone else or had fabricated it of his own accord. He said: ﴿So I had remained among you a lifetime before it.﴾ You know my condition, and my journeys, my comings and goings, my truthfulness and my trustworthiness are not hidden from you. For this reason I was never able to say anything of it at all, nor had any knowledge of it or of any part of it. Then I brought it to you suddenly, without effort, without learning, and without the means by which I could have acquired it or any part of it. This is among the clearest evidences and most manifest proofs that it is from God; He revealed it to me and sent it down upon me. Had He willed, He would not have done so: He would not have enabled me to recite it, nor enabled you to know it. Rather, He enabled me to recite it and enabled you to know it, so you did not know it nor any part of it, and before it was revealed to me I was not reciting it nor any part of it. So consider the soundness of this proof, the excellence of its composition, and the clarity of its indication.

From this is His, glory be to Him, saying: ﴿And if We willed, We would surely take away what We revealed to you; then you would not find for yourself any guardian against Us in respect to it.﴾

This is the fitting one to match His saying: ﴿Or do they say, "He has fabricated against God a lie"? If God willed, He would seal upon your heart,﴾ and His saying: ﴿And if he had fabricated against Us some sayings, We would have seized him by the right hand.﴾ And it is an independent proof mentioned in the Qur'an in several ways. And God knows best.

Eighth, such a construction in the Qur'an comes only for negation, not for affirmation, as in His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And if We willed, We would surely take away what We revealed to you.﴾ And His saying: ﴿If He wills, He will take you away, O people, and bring others.﴾ And His saying: ﴿If He wills, He will still the wind, and they would remain motionless on its back.﴾ And His saying: ﴿If We will, We will cause the earth to swallow them, or drop upon them a piece of the sky.﴾ And its counterparts. It has come only where what follows the verb of will is negated.

The ninth point: sealing the heart does not necessitate patience. Rather, a servant's heart may be sealed and his patience taken from him. Indeed, when the heart is sealed, patience disappears and weakens. This differs from binding (rabt) upon the heart, which does necessitate patience, as Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And He sends down upon you water from the sky to purify you by it, remove from you the defilement of Satan, and strengthen your hearts﴾. In the language, rabt means tying or binding, and so it is said of anyone who endures a matter that he "bound his heart," as if he restrained his heart from agitation. From this comes the expression "he is steadfast of heart" (rabit al-jash).

Al-Wahidi thought that (ʿalā) is superfluous, and that the meaning is "He binds your hearts." That is not what he supposed. There is a clear difference between binding a thing and binding upon it. One says rabata al-faras and al-dabbah (he tied the horse and the animal), and one does not say rabata ʿalayha. When the binding surrounds and covers a thing, it is said rabata ʿalayhi, as if he had encompassed it with the binding. Therefore it is said rabata ʿalā qalbihi, which is more eloquent than saying rabata qalbahu. The point is that with this binding comes stronger and more enduring patience, unlike sealing.

The tenth point: sealing (khatm) is the fastening of the heart so that it does not perceive or understand. It is a barrier preventing knowledge and intention. The Prophet (ﷺ) knew the words of his enemies that he had fabricated the Qur'an, and he perceived them. Allah did not place upon his heart a barrier preventing him from perceiving that or knowing it.

If it is said that the matter is so, but that Allah placed upon his heart a barrier preventing harm from their words, this is more fitting to be called a sealing. Their words did harm him and grieved them, as Allah the Exalted says: ﴿We know that what they say grieves you﴾. The arrival of this harm to him was from Allah's honour toward him, for no prophet was harmed as he was harmed. The interpretation of the verse is the view of Qatadah, and Allah knows best.

Then Allah the Exalted informed that the Qur'an is a reminder (tadhkirah) for the God-fearing (muttaqin), by which the God-fearing one is reminded, sees what benefits him so that he pursues it, and what harms him so that he avoids it. By it he is reminded of the names, attributes and actions of the Lord, so that he believes. By it he is reminded of His reward and punishment, His threat and command, His prohibition, and His signs in His friends and His enemies, in himself, and in what purifies, cleanses and elevates it, and in what corrupts, conceals and debases it. By it he is reminded of the knowledge of origin and return, of Paradise and Hellfire, and of the knowledge of good and evil. It is therefore the reminder in reality, a proof for the worlds and a benefit and guidance for those who seek knowledge.

Then He, glorified is He, said: ﴿And indeed We know that among you are deniers﴾, meaning: they are not hidden from Us, and We will repay them for their denial.

Then Allah the Exalted informed that His Messenger and His speech are a cause of anguish (hasrah) for the disbelievers when they witness the reality of what he reported. Their denial will be among the greatest of their regrets, when regret will no longer benefit them. Thus is every one who denies the truth and affirms falsehood: when the reality of what he denied and affirmed is revealed to him, his denial and affirmation become a regret for him, like one who neglected what would benefit him at the time of acquiring it, until his need for it becomes intense and he witnesses the success of those who attained it, and his neglect becomes a regret upon him.

Then Allah the Exalted informed that the Qur'an and the Messenger are *ḥaqq al-yaqīn* (the sure truth of certainty). It is said that this is of the type of annexing a qualified noun to its quality, meaning "the true certainty," like *masjid al-jāmiʿ* and *ṣalāt al-ūlā*. This point requires verification, so we say, and with Allah is success.

(Section)

Allah the Exalted mentioned in His Book the degrees of certainty (yaqin), and they are three: *ḥaqq al-yaqīn* (the truth of certainty), *ʿilm al-yaqīn* (the knowledge of certainty), and *ʿayn al-yaqīn* (the eye of certainty), as Allah the Exalted says: ﴿No! If you knew with the knowledge of certainty, you would surely see the Hellfire; then you would surely see it with the eye of certainty﴾. These are three degrees of certainty. The first is its knowledge, which is complete affirmation without any doubt or uncertainty that undermines that affirmation, such as the knowledge of certainty about Paradise, for example, and their certainty that it is the abode of the God-fearing and the dwelling of the believers. This is the level of knowledge, like their certainty that the messengers reported it from Allah, and their certainty of the truthfulness of the one who reports.

The second degree is *ʿayn al-yaqīn*, which is the level of seeing and witnessing, as Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Then you would surely see it with the eye of certainty﴾. Between this degree and the one before it there is the difference between knowledge and witnessing: certainty belongs to hearing, and the eye of certainty belongs to sight. In the Musnad of Imam Ahmad, it is related from the Prophet (ﷺ) as a marfūʿ report: "The report is not like one who witnesses it." This is the degree which Abraham the Friend (al-Khalil) asked his Lord to show him, how He gives life to the dead, so that he might attain, alongside knowledge of certainty, the eye of certainty. His request was an increase for himself and a reassurance for his heart, so that the heart is at rest at the moment of witnessing and is content by closing the distance between report and seeing. It is upon this distance that the Prophet used the word "doubt," when he said: "We have more right to doubt than Abraham." Far be it that there was any doubt, either in Abraham or in anyone else. Rather, it is the eye after knowledge, witnessing after report, and sight after hearing.

The third degree is *ḥaqq al-yaqīn*, which is direct contact with a thing through perception of it, as when they enter Paradise and enjoy what is in it. In this world they are at the level of *ʿilm al-yaqīn*; on the Day of Standing, as they draw near and are brought close until they witness it, they are at the level of *ʿayn al-yaqīn*; and when they enter it and experience its bliss, they are at the level of *ḥaqq al-yaqīn*. Direct contact with the known object sometimes occurs through the outward senses and sometimes through the heart. Therefore Allah says: ﴿And indeed, it is the truth of certainty﴾. The heart directly experiences faith in it and mingles with it, just as it directly experiences by the senses what is connected to them. Then the brightness of it mixes with the hearts, and *ḥaqq al-yaqīn* remains for them. This is the highest level of faith, which is the state of *ṣiddīqiyyah* (truthfulness), in which the ranks of believers differ.

Some scholars gave an example for the three degrees. He said: If someone whose truthfulness you are certain of tells you, "I have honey, and I want to feed you some of it," and you believe him, that is *ʿilm al-yaqīn*. When he brings it before you, that is *ʿayn al-yaqīn*. When you taste it, that is *ḥaqq al-yaqīn*.

On this basis, this annexation is not of the type of a qualified noun to its quality, but rather of the type of annexing a genus to its species. *ʿIlm*, *ʿayn* and *ḥaqq* are more general than being certainty, so the general is annexed to the specific, like "some of the goods" and "all the dirhams." Since the annexing word and the annexed word in this construction both refer to one and the same entity, unlike your saying "the house of ʿAmr" or "the garment of Zayd," those who thought it was annexing a qualified noun to its quality were mistaken. Rather, it is of the type of annexing a genus to its species, like "a garment of silk" and "a ring of silver." The annexed term may be different from the annexing term, so they do not refer to one entity; or it may be homogeneous with it, so they refer to one named thing. And Allah knows best.

Then He concluded the surah with His saying: ﴿So glorify the name of your Lord, the Mighty﴾.

It is fitting for this conclusion, because it contains information about the greatness and majesty of the Lord, the mention of the immensity of His dominion, the operation of His judgment with justice over His servants in this world and the Hereafter, and the mention of His greatness in sending His Messenger and sending down His Book. He is greater, more glorious and more magnificent in the eyes of the people of His heavens and the believers among His servants than to approve a lie attributed to Him and fabricated against Him, one that alters His religion, abrogates His laws, kills His servants, and reports about Him what has no reality. Yet He, glorified is He, supports and aids him, answers his supplications, seizes his enemies, raises his station and exalts his remembrance. He is the Mighty, whose greatness refuses to do such a thing to one who comes with the vilest kinds of lying and wrongdoing. So glorified is our Lord, the Mighty, and exalted far above what the ignorant attribute to Him, a great exaltation.

That is, if he had brought something of his own accord, We would have seized him by the right hand, cut the aorta of his heart, and destroyed him. God has protected him from inclining toward his enemies even by a particle of his heart, and from fabricating speech against Him, glory be to Him. How many have inclined toward his enemies and fabricated speech against Him from their own selves, and He gave them respite and paid them no heed, like all the people of innovation (ahl al-bid'ah, those who introduce novelties into religion), who fabricate against His names, attributes, and religion.

He also said in *al-Madarij* (*Madarij al-Salikin*):

When you contemplate the Qur'an, you see it calling out to this, displaying it and repeating it for those who have understanding and a heart that is attentive to God. God, exalted is He, said: ﴿And if he had fabricated against Us some sayings, We would have seized him by the right hand, then We would have cut from him the aorta, and none of you could have held Us off from him.﴾

Do you not see how He, glory be to Him, informs us that His perfection, His wisdom, and His power refuse to let stand one who fabricates some sayings against Him? Rather, He must make him an example to His servants, as His sunnah has run concerning those who fabricate against Him.

He also said in *al-Tibyan fi Aqsam al-Qur'an* (*al-Tibyan*):

Then, glory be to Him, He established a decisive proof of the truthfulness of His Messenger, and that he did not fabricate against Him in what he said, and that if he had fabricated against Him, He would not have approved it and would have hastened his destruction. For the perfection of His knowledge, power, and wisdom refuses to let stand one who fabricates against Him, forges lies about Him, leads His servants astray, permits the blood of those who denied him, their honor, and their property, spreads corruption, tyranny, and falsehood on earth, and opposes creation. How then could it befit the Wisest of the wise, the Most Merciful of the merciful, and the Most Capable of the capable to let him stand in this? Rather, how could it befit Him to support him, help him, exalt him, make him prevail, and grant him victory over the people of truth, while he sheds their blood, permits their property, their children, and their women, saying: "God commanded me to do this and permitted it to me"? Rather, how could it befit Him to confirm him with every kind of confirmation: confirming him by approving him, by the signs that necessarily imply his truthfulness, whose indication of confirmation is like the indication of confirmation by speech, which is manifest. Then He confirms him by all their kinds in their variety, so that each sign on its own confirms him, and then through the combination of those signs there arises a confirmation above the confirmation of each sign individually. Then creation is unable to oppose him. Then He confirms him by His speech and His word, then establishes the decisive proof that this is His word and His speech, bearing witness to him by His approval, His action, and His word. It is therefore among the greatest impossibilities, the most false of falsehoods, and the clearest of slander, that the Wisest of the wise and Lord of the worlds should permit such a thing to be done to the liar who fabricates against Him, who is the worst of creation absolutely. Whoever permits God to do this to the worst and most lying of His creatures has certainly not believed in God, nor known God, and this is not the Lord of the worlds. It is not fitting to attribute this to anyone who has a grain of intellect, wisdom, and reason. Whoever does this has disgraced himself and proclaimed his own ignorance.

I recall a debate that took place between me and some Jews. After I had argued at length for the prophethood of the Prophet, I said to him: "Denying his prophethood entails disparaging the Lord of the worlds and belittling Him in the most abominable way." He said: "How can you say such a thing?" I said: "Its explanation is up to me. Now listen: you claim that he was not a messenger, but rather a dominant king who subdued people by his sword until they submitted to him. He remained for twenty-three years lying against God, saying, 'It was revealed to me,' when nothing had been revealed to him; 'He commanded me,' when He had not commanded him; 'He forbade me,' when He had not forbidden him; and he said, 'God said such-and-such,' when He had not said it; and he made lawful such-and-such, forbade such-and-such, made obligatory such-and-such, and made reprehensible such-and-such, when He had not made any of these lawful, forbidden, obligatory, or reprehensible. Rather, he did all of that of his own accord, lying and fabricating against God, and against His prophets, His messengers, and His angels. Then he remained for thirteen years after that, going about among His servants, shedding their blood, seizing their property, enslaving their women and children, though they had committed no offense except rejecting him and opposing him, and in all of this he kept saying, 'God commanded me to do this,' when He had not commanded him. Moreover, he strove to change the religions of the messengers, abrogate their laws, and dissolve their sacred ordinances. This is his condition according to you. Then either the Lord, exalted is He, knew of all this and was informed of his condition, seeing it and witnessing it, or He did not. If you say that all of this was hidden from God, unknown to Him, then you have attributed to the Lord, exalted is He, an extreme ignorance, for He did not become aware of this tremendous event, nor know it, nor see it. If you say rather that it happened with His knowledge, His awareness, and His witnessing, it is said to you: was He able to change that, to seize his hand and to come between him and it, or not? If you say He was not able to do so, then you attribute to Him an incapacity that contradicts lordship, and this man and his followers would have been more capable than He of carrying out their will. If you say rather that He was able, but He empowered him, supported him, and gave him dominion over creation, and did not help His friends and the followers of His messengers, then you attribute to Him the greatest folly, injustice, and failure to uphold wisdom. This would hold even if He had merely left him free to do what he did; how much more so when, in all of that, He is his helper and supporter, answers his supplications, destroys those who opposed and denied him, confirms him in every kind of confirmation, and manifests signs through his hands, which if all the people of the earth gathered to produce one of them, they could not, and they would be unable to do so."

And every moment there happens to him, from the causes of victory, empowerment, manifestation, exaltation, and the multiplication of followers, something beyond the ordinary. Thus it becomes clear that whoever denies that he was a messenger and a prophet has blamed God, disparaged Him, and attributed to Him ignorance, incapacity, and folly.

I said to him: "This is not undermined by the tyrannical kings whom God empowered on earth for a time, and then cut off their root, nullified their sunnah, and erased their traces and their oppression. For those did not bring anything of this kind, nor were they supported and helped, nor did signs appear at their hands, nor did the Lord, exalted is He, confirm them by His approval, by His action, or by His word. Rather, their command was the opposite of the Messenger's command, like Pharaoh, Nimrod, and their likes. Nor is this undermined by those who claimed prophethood among the liars, for their condition was the opposite of the Messenger's condition in every respect. Rather, their condition is among the clearest proofs of the Messenger's truthfulness. Among God's wisdom, glory be to Him, is that He brought such people into existence so that the condition of the liars and the condition of the truthful might be known, and their appearance was among the clearest evidences for the truthfulness of the messengers. The difference between these and those is shown by their opposites, and things are made clear by their opposites. Thus knowledge of the proofs of falsehood and its confusions is among the kinds of proofs of truth and its demonstrations."

When he heard this, he said: "God forbid! We do not say that he was a tyrannical king, but a noble prophet, and whoever follows him is among the happy. Likewise, whoever follows Moses is like one who follows Muhammad."

I said to him: "Everything you disguise by this is null. For if you acknowledge that he is a truthful prophet, then it is necessary to affirm him in everything he reported. His followers and his enemies alike know by necessity that he called all people to faith, and informed that whoever does not believe in him is an unbeliever destined for the Fire, and that he fought those of the People of the Book who did not believe in him, branded them with disbelief, and permitted their property, their blood, their women, and their children. If that was an aggression and an injustice on his part, then he was not a prophet, and the matter returns to disparagement of the Lord, exalted is He. If that was by God's command and His revelation, then no one may oppose him, abandon his followers, and it is binding to affirm him in what he reported and obey him in what he commanded."

Glory be to Him has pointed to this kingship in more than one place in His Book. He said: ﴿And if he had fabricated against Us some sayings, We would have seized him by the right hand, then We would have cut from him the aorta, and none of you could have held Us off from him.﴾

He, glory be to Him, says: If he had fabricated against Us a single saying of his own accord, which We did not say and did not reveal to him, We would not have let it stand; We would have seized him by his right hand and then destroyed him. This is one of the two opinions. Ibn Qutaybah said: there are two opinions on this. One is that "the right hand" means strength and power, and the right hand is used in place of strength, because the strength of everything is in its right side. I say: according to this, "the right hand" is a description of the seizing, and this is the view of Ibn Abbas regarding "the right hand."

He said: The lexicographers have another interpretation of this. It is that the speech follows what people are accustomed to, namely taking a man by the hand when they want to punish him. They say, when they wish to punish a man, "Take his hand," and the sultan and the judge most often say this after the verdict has become due: "Take his hand, seize his hand."
